title: Consonant Digraphs
keyIdea: A consonant digraph is two letters that make one sound: sh in ship, ch in chip, th in bath, ng in ring and ck in duck. Count sounds, not letters, so duck has 4 letters but 3 sounds. ph says f, as in photo, and wh says w, as in wheel. At the end of a short word, straight after a short vowel, the k sound is spelled ck (duck) and the ch sound is spelled tch (match). After a consonant it is just k or ch: milk, lunch.

kid: Some letters work as a team. s and h stick together and say sh. Ship is sh, i, p. One team, one sound.
Teams to know: sh in ship, ch in chip, th in bath, ng in ring and ck in duck. Ship and chip look the same at the end. The team at the start makes them two words.
Two teams play a trick. p and h say f, like in photo. w and h say w, like in wheel. Count sounds, not letters. Duck has 4 letters. Say it slowly: d, u, ck. That is 3 sounds.
Duck ends in ck, and match ends in tch. That is because a short vowel sound comes just before. Milk ends in k, as l comes just before.
adult: A consonant digraph is two letters that spell one consonant phoneme. Year 1 of the English national curriculum teaches ch, sh, th, ng and ck, the /k/ sound spelt ck after a single short vowel, tch for /tʃ/ after a single short vowel (with exceptions such as rich, which, much and such), ph and wh in words like dolphin and wheel, and k rather than c before e, i and y (kit, skip). Common Core RF.1.3a asks children to know the spelling-sound links for common consonant digraphs.

Key words: phoneme (one sound), grapheme (the letter or letters that spell it), digraph (two letters, one sound), trigraph (three letters, one sound, such as tch), and sound buttons: a dot under a single letter and a line under a digraph. Children who segment by sound can spell; those who count letters cannot.

Common mistakes: reading the two letters apart (s-h-i-p), which breaks the word; counting letters instead of sounds; reading ph as p; hearing sh in any word that starts with s, such as snake; and writing duk for duck or mach for match. Be careful with th: it has a quiet sound in thin and a buzzy sound in that, but it is the same digraph.

In the lab your child drags sh, ch or th into a word and lets the picture decide (ship or chip), counts sounds in duck, ring and chick, sorts ph and wh words by the sound they make, chooses ck or k and tch or ch to finish a word, and hunts the pictures that start with sh. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Go on a sound hunt at home. Find three things that start with sh, ch or th: a shoe, a chair, a thumb. Say each one slowly and ask: is it one sound or two at the start?

visual.caption: Which team starts the word? Drag each word, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag digraph magnets into words, count sounds not letters, sort ph and wh, pick ck or tch endings and hunt for sh.

practice.prompt: Which two letters make one sound in fish?
practice.hint: Say fish slowly. Listen for the sound at the end.
practice.explain: s and h team up to say sh. Fish has 3 sounds: f, i, sh.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters. One pair of letters is a team, like ck in duck. How many sounds does the word have?
practice.hint: Each letter makes a sound, but the team of two makes only one. Take 1 away.
practice.explain: The two team letters share one sound, so {n} letters make {=n-1} sounds. Duck has 4 letters and 3 sounds.

practice.prompt: What sound does ph make in dolphin?
practice.hint: p and h are a team. Say dolphin out loud.
practice.explain: ph says f, so dolphin sounds like dol-fin. It does not say p.

practice.prompt: Ship has 3 sounds: sh-i-p. You read {n} words like ship. How many sounds do you say in all?
practice.hint: Each word like ship has 3 sounds. Count 3 for each word.
practice.explain: {n} words with 3 sounds each make {=3*n} sounds. The sh counts as one sound each time.

pool.prompt: How many sounds are in chip?
pool.hint: c and h are a team. Count sounds, not letters.
pool.explain: Chip has 3 sounds: ch, i, p. The c and h make one sound, and the i must not be skipped.

pool.hint: Listen to the vowel just before the k sound. Is it short?
pool.explain: Duck has a short u just before the k sound, so it ends in ck.

pool.hint: sh sounds like a quiet finger on your lips: shh.
pool.explain: Sheep starts with sh. Sun starts with s on its own, and cheese starts with ch.

pool.prompt: What sound does wh make in wheel?
pool.hint: w and h are a team. Say wheel out loud.
pool.explain: wh says w, so wheel starts with a w sound. The two letters make one sound.

pool.prompt: A little stick that lights a fire. Which spelling is right?
pool.hint: The a in match is short. What comes after a short vowel?
pool.explain: After a short vowel, the ch sound is spelled tch: match, catch, fetch.

pool.hint: ng is the sound at the end of sing.
pool.explain: Ring ends with ng, one sound. Rig ends with g, and rich ends with ch.

pool.prompt: Chick has 5 letters but only 3 sounds, because ch and ck are teams. A word has {n} letters and two teams. How many sounds does it have?
pool.hint: Each team of two letters makes one sound. Two teams means take 2 away.
pool.explain: Two teams save 2 sounds, so {n} letters make {=n-2} sounds. Chick: ch, i, ck.

pool.prompt: Mia draws one line under each team of two letters. She draws {n} lines for words like sh, ch and th. How many letters are in her teams?
pool.hint: Each team has 2 letters. Count 2 for each line.
pool.explain: {n} teams of 2 letters make {=2*n} letters, but only {n} sounds.

pool.prompt: Which word ends in just k, not ck?
pool.hint: Look at the letter just before the k sound. Is it a vowel or a consonant?
pool.explain: In milk, l comes just before the k sound, so it is just k. Duck and sock have a short vowel before, so they use ck.
